column1: # C files deliberately kept inside a library that already has a build.zig.
# Enforced by scripts/checks/check_zig_parallel_trees.py, so a port that
# leaves C behind has to say so here instead of leaving a parallel tree.
# A .c under a library's tests/ needs no row: C test fixtures are how the Zig
# is held to the C ABI, and they are deliberately C.

column3: Compile-time conformance TU for the fw_os port contract; a header with no translation unit behind it is never compiled and rots.

The neutral clock-intent port, landed on dev in #693 and carried onto this branch by the zig/dev sync below it. libs/if is migrated here but not on dev, so dev can add C to it without seeing this checker; the row is what the sync owes. Ports with the rest of the if surface.

Emits the NS image's ra8_ns_rot_header_t record; stays C on purpose, as tests/cmake/zig_libraries.cmake records, so the magic word and struct shape are compiler-checked instead of hand-assembled in the NS linker scripts.

column1: # ra8_jpeg is partially migrated: the ra8_imgdec backend binding is Zig
# the codec proper is still C. Five TUs, one shared internal header, one block.

column3: Decoder core of the baseline codec: the marker walk and the SOF/SOS/DHT/DQT table state behind src/ra8_jpeg_sw_internal.h. The encoder left for Zig in #2795; these three decoder TUs share that header and the stripe cursor by value, so they port as one block rather than piecemeal.

Whole-buffer baseline decoder: Huffman tables, the dequantise and IDCT path, upsampling. Shares src/ra8_jpeg_sw_internal.h and its decode state with ra8_jpeg_sw.c and ra8_jpeg_sw_stream.c, so it ports with them; the imgdec seam went in #2786 and the encoder in #2795.

Bounded-memory striped decoder driving the same core as the whole-buffer path. Holds the stripe cursor across calls through src/ra8_jpeg_sw_internal.h, so splitting it from the other two decoder TUs would put shared decoder state across a language boundary mid-port.

column1: # ra8_dfu is partially migrated: the polled USB-DFU host driver is Zig
# (#2809), the rest of the library is still C. Six TUs, three blocks.

column3: Reset-time boot decision: software CRC32, image-header validation and A/B slot selection. No MMIO, and the only ra8_dfu TU with host unit tests behind it, so it ports with its suite rather than ahead of it.

SRAM-resident MRAM program/verify of the inactive slot over ra8_flash. Linked into a .sram_text section by cmake/ra8_app/sources.cmake so it cannot execute from the MRAM it erases; a Zig object has to be placed the same way, which is a linker-script change this slice does not make.

USBX DFU device class bound to real MRAM through the ux_dcd_ra8_usb bridge. Its seam is the vendored USBX callback surface rather than ra8_usb_host_*, so it ports after the host side proves the pattern (#2809).

Copy-to-run launch gate: verifies the slot's ECDSA-P256 signature via ra8_psa_crypto, then branches to the run base. Shares the anti-rollback counter with ra8_dfu_antirollback.c and ra8_rot.c, so those three port as one block.
Monotonic anti-rollback counter behind the launch gate. Shares its record layout with ra8_dfu_launch.c and ra8_rot.c; splitting it would put that record across a language boundary mid-port.

Root-of-trust key reader, also compiled directly by three HIL examples through EXTRA_SRCS rather than through the library. Ports with ra8_dfu_launch.c and ra8_dfu_antirollback.c once those examples can take an archive.

column1: # ra8_core is partially migrated: the freestanding runtime primitives are
# Zig (#2820), the other sixteen TUs are still C. Four blocks.

column3: Millisecond timebase. The counter and the delay are ordinary code, but the firmware-only SysTick_Handler in this TU dispatches through three weak externs (_tx_timer_interrupt, ux_dcd_ra8_usb_irq_reenable, g_ra8_threadx_systick_ready) and is itself a weak definition the vector table's alias loses to and an app's own handler wins over. That behaviour is the ELF linker's, not the compiler's: a wrong port does not fail a build, it stops ThreadX ticking on a board. It ports in a slice that can be checked against a full ARM image link with and without libthreadx.a, or against hardware. The rest of the timebase went to Zig in #2830.

Reset-time region descriptor read, placed in a .boot_text section by the linker script so it runs before the MRAM regions it describes are mapped. A Zig object has to be placed the same way, which is a linker-script change no ra8_core slice has made yet.
TrustZone secure-world entry veneers. The cmse non-secure-call attributes have no Zig spelling yet, and #591 left the secure-world seam Brighton's call rather than this lane's.
Deterministic RNG stub the host suites substitute for the hardware TRNG. Its whole purpose is being swapped at link time by the test build, so it ports with the TRNG driver rather than alone.

Traps any heap allocation the toolchain emits, so a newlib _sbrk call fails the link loudly instead of silently growing a heap. It exists to answer a libc symbol at link time and is a five-line TU; it ports with whatever slice retires the last libc seam.
